<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par73 />{{GHGterm|Yôdh}} in Arabic) ''to comprehend, to measure'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִיט}} (as in Arabic and Syriac) ''to rush upon'', and the denominative {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=קָץ}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫יִץ}}) ''to pass the summer'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=6}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=וְדִיגוּם|translate=and they shall fish them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=16}}, generally explained as {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}}, denominative from {{GHGheb|text=דָּג|translate=fish}}, probably represents a denominative {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְדִיְגוּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|c}}
Corresponding to verbs properly {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}}, mentioned in {{GHGpar|72|gg}}, there are certain verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} with consonantal {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, as {{GHGheb|text=אָיַב|translate=to hate}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָיֵף|translate=to faint}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה|translate=to become, to be}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָיָה|translate=to live}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|d}}
Rem. 1. In the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} 3rd ''fem. sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְלָ֫נֶה}} occurs once, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=4}}, for {{GHGheb|text=וְלָ֫נָה}}, with the weakening of the toneless ''ā'' to ''ĕ'' (as in the ''fem. participle'' {{GHGheb|text=זוּרֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=5}}); cf. the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|48|l}} and {{GHGpar|80|i}}.—2nd ''sing. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=שַׁתָּ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=8}}, {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}; cf. {{GHGpar|72|s}}); 1st ''sing.'' once {{GHGheb|text=שַׁתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=28}}, ''milraʿ'', without any apparent reason; 1st ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְלַ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=13}} for ''lán-nû''. The lengthened {{GHGterm|imperative}} has the tone on the ultima before gutturals, {{GHGheb|text=רִיבָ֫ה יהוה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=1}}; see further, {{GHGpar|72|s}}.—Examples of the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} are: {{GHGheb|text=רֹב|translate=litigando}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׂוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁת|translate=ponendo}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=7}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=דִיב יָדִיב}} (for {{GHGheb|text=דֹב}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=34}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּין תָּבִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=חול תחיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, are irregular and perhaps due to incorrect ''scriptio plena''; for the last the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} requires {{GHGheb|text=הוּל תָּחוּל}}, but read {{GHGheb|text=חוֹל}}; cf. {{GHGpar|113|x}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|e}}
2. The ''shortened imperfect'' usually has the form {{GHGheb|text=יָבֵן}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׂם}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁת}}; more rarely, with the tone moved back, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫רֶב לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=31}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תָּ֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=20}}. So with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫שֶׂם|translate=and he placed}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫בֶן|translate=and he perceived}}; with a middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫עַט בָּהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=14}} (see {{GHGpar|72|ee}}); with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} as 3rd radical, {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּ֫שַׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=1}}. As jussive of {{GHGheb|text=לִין}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּלַ֫ן}} is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=20}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=2}}, for {{GHGheb|text=תָּלֵן}}.—For {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תָּרוֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=30}} ''Keth.'' (''Q<sup>e</sup>re'' {{GHGheb|text=תָּרִיב}}) read {{GHGheb|text=תָּרֵב}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|f}}
3. As ''participle active Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=לֵן|translate=spending the night}}, occurs once, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=21}}; {{GHGterm|participle passive}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=4}}; ''feminine'' {{GHGheb|text=שׂוּמָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=32}}, in the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, even according to the reading of the Oriental schools (see p. 38, note 2): the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} has {{GHGheb|text=שִׂימָה}}. A {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}} (cf. above, {{GHGpar|52|e}} and s, and {{GHGpar|53|u}}) from {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים}} may perhaps be seen in {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫ישֶׂם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=26}} (also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=33}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=ויישם}}, {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוּשָׂם}}; the Samaritan in both places has {{GHGheb|text=ויושם}}), and also in {{GHGheb|text=יִיסָךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=32}}, Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=יוסך}}. Against the explanation of {{GHGheb|text=ייסך}} as a {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}-form from {{GHGheb|text=סוּךְ}}, Barth ({{GHGcite|title=Jubelschrift... Hildesheimer}}, Berlin, 1890, p. 151) rightly urges that the only example of a Hiphʿîl of {{GHGheb|text=סוּךְ}} is the doubtful {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫םֶךְ}}, which is probably an ''ĭ''-imperfect of {{GHGterm|Qal}}.—The explanation of {{GHGheb|text=יישם}}, &c., as a {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}} arising from ''yiysam'', &c. = ''yuysam'' (so Barth, ibid., note 1), is certainly also unconvincing, so that the correctness of the traditional reading is open to question.

{{center|<nowiki>* * * * * *</nowiki>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|g}}
4. In verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״א}} the {{GHGheb|text=א}} always retains its censonantal value; these stems are, therefore, to be regarded as verbs ''middle Guttural'' (§ 64). An exception is {{GHGheb|text=יָנֵאץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=5}} if it be {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=נאץ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יַנְאֵץ}}); but if the form has really been correctly transmitted, it should rather be referred to {{GHGheb|text=נָצַץ}}, and regarded as incorrectly written for {{GHGheb|text=יָנֵץ}}. On {{GHGheb|text=נָאווּ}} (from {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲוָה}}), which was formerly treated here as {{GHGheb|text=ע״א}}, see now {{GHGpar|75|x}}.<section end=par73 /><noinclude>
